newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK, USA sign agreements to battle crime.
newsitem.headline: HK, USA sign agreements to battle crime.

text.p: Hong Kong and the United States signed two agreements on Tuesday that provide legal assistance in criminal cases and allow people to serve sentences in their home country.
The Agreement on the Transfer of Sentenced Persons (TSP) is the first such pact Hong Kong has signed, the Hong Kong government said in a statement.
The deal on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters (MLA) is the second such agreement that Hong Kong has inked. The first was with Australia in September 1996.
Assistance extended under the MLA includes the taking of evidence, searching for and seizing items relevant to criminal cases, and producing documentary evidence.

Speaking at the signing ceremony, Hong Kong's secretary for security, Peter Lai, said: "Hong Kong is a major law enforcement partner of the U.S. in East Asia and our government is determined to continue this partnership."
Under the TSP agreement, the convict must consent to the transfer. Any adjustment to the sentence by the originating jurisdiction must also be adhered to by the receiving country, it said.
The agreements have been endorsed by the joint Sino-British body handling the details of Hong Kong's July 1 transfer to Chinese rule.
